q: Name a person who created or co-designed a programming language.
hint: Designers of general-purpose, shell, query, teaching or esoteric languages count. Markup, frameworks and runtimes don't.

answers.l: Started Python as a hobby project over Christmas 1989 and named it after Monty Python's Flying Circus.
Created C at Bell Labs in the early 1970s and used it to rewrite Unix.
Began C with Classes at Bell Labs in 1979; it was renamed C++ in 1983.
Led the Sun project that produced Oak in 1991, renamed Java before its 1995 release.
Wrote the first JavaScript prototype at Netscape in about ten days in May 1995.
Released Perl 1.0 in 1987 while working as a programmer at Unisys, and later led the design of Raku.
Released Ruby in 1995, with the stated goal of making programmers happy.
Released Personal Home Page Tools in 1995, the start of PHP.
Wrote Turbo Pascal, was chief architect of Delphi, then designed C# and TypeScript at Microsoft.
Created B at Bell Labs around 1969, the direct ancestor of C, and later co-designed Go at Google.
Co-designed Go at Google starting in 2007; earlier created Newsqueak and co-designed Limbo.
Invented Lisp at MIT in 1958 and coined the term artificial intelligence.
Designed Pascal (1970), Modula-2 and Oberon at ETH Zurich; received the 1984 Turing Award.
Started Swift at Apple in 2010, unveiled in 2014; also created LLVM and later Mojo.
Started Rust as a personal project in 2006 while at Mozilla, which began sponsoring it in 2009.
Led development of FLOW-MATIC, an English-like business language that strongly shaped COBOL.
Led the IBM team that delivered FORTRAN in 1957; Backus-Naur form is named partly for him.
Led the Xerox PARC group that created Smalltalk in the 1970s.
Created Scala at EPFL, first released in 2004; earlier co-designed Generic Java.
Released Clojure, a Lisp dialect for the JVM, in 2007.
Created Elixir, first released in 2012, to run on the Erlang VM; he was previously on the Rails core team.
One of Go's three original designers at Google, alongside Rob Pike and Ken Thompson.
Key designer of Haskell and lead developer of the Glasgow Haskell Compiler for decades.
Co-created BASIC at Dartmouth College in 1964 with Thomas Kurtz.
Co-created BASIC with John Kemeny; the first BASIC program ran at Dartmouth on May 1, 1964.
Created APL, introduced in his 1962 book A Programming Language; received the 1979 Turing Award.
Created Forth, a stack-based language, around 1970; it was used early on for telescope control at NRAO.
Created Tcl in 1988 at UC Berkeley as an embeddable command language for tools.
Created the D language, first released in 2001; earlier wrote the Zortech C++ compiler.
Designed F# at Microsoft Research, first released in 2005.
Created ML in the 1970s as the meta language for the LCF theorem prover; 1991 Turing Award.
Co-created Scheme with Guy Steele at MIT in 1975 and co-wrote SICP.
Co-created Scheme with Gerald Sussman, wrote Common Lisp the Language, and led Fortress at Sun.
Co-created R with Robert Gentleman at the University of Auckland in the early 1990s.
Co-created R with Ross Ihaka; their shared first initial is one reason for the name.
Created the Wolfram Language, released as the core of Mathematica in 1988.
Wrote the first MATLAB in the late 1970s so students could use LINPACK and EISPACK without Fortran.
Co-created Logo in 1967 with Wally Feurzeig and Cynthia Solomon, later known for turtle graphics.
Designed TeX, whose macro language is Turing complete, and the MIX assembly language used in TAOCP.
Designed CLU at MIT in the mid 1970s, a language built around abstract data types; 2008 Turing Award.
Designed Eiffel in 1986 and coined the term Design by Contract.
Created Objective-C in the early 1980s with Tom Love, adding Smalltalk-style messaging to C.
Lead architect of Lua, created in 1993 at PUC-Rio in Brazil.
Created Zig, announced in 2016, and leads the Zig Software Foundation.
Co-created Erlang at Ericsson in 1986 for telephone switching systems.
Created CoffeeScript in 2009; also wrote Backbone.js and Underscore.js.
Wrote the Bourne shell, released with Version 7 Unix in 1979; its syntax borrows from ALGOL 68.
The K in AWK, created at Bell Labs in 1977 with Alfred Aho and Peter Weinberger.
Lead designer of Kotlin at JetBrains, unveiled in 2011.
Created Prolog in Marseille in 1972 with Philippe Roussel.
Co-created Simula, the first object-oriented language, with Ole-Johan Dahl in Oslo in the 1960s.
Co-designed Simula 67 with Kristen Nygaard; the pair shared the 2001 Turing Award.
Wrote the C shell at Berkeley in the late 1970s, along with vi, and later co-founded Sun.
Wrote Bash for the GNU Project, first released in 1989.
Led the Green team at CII Honeywell Bull whose design was chosen as Ada in 1979.
Lead developer of OCaml at INRIA, first released in 1996; also created the CompCert verified C compiler.
Created Elm, a functional language for web front ends, as his senior thesis in 2012.
Co-created Dart at Google, announced in 2011; earlier led the V8 JavaScript engine.
Co-created Julia, publicly announced in 2012, while a graduate student at MIT.
Co-created Julia with Jeff Bezanson, Viral Shah and Alan Edelman.
Designed Plankalkül in the 1940s, often called the first high-level programming language.
Designed Arc, a Lisp dialect released in 2008 with Robert Morris; co-founded Y Combinator.
Created QuakeC, the language used for game logic in Quake (1996).
Created Brainfuck in 1993, aiming for the smallest possible compiler on the Amiga.
Member of the committee that designed Haskell and co-designer of Generic Java, the basis for Java generics.
Designed and implemented much of Smalltalk at Xerox PARC in the 1970s.
Co-developed Smalltalk-80 at Xerox PARC and co-wrote the book that defined it.
Led the creation of S at Bell Labs starting in 1976, the language R was modeled on.
The A in AWK; also co-wrote the Dragon Book on compilers and shared the 2020 Turing Award.
Created Groovy in 2003, a dynamic language for the JVM.
Co-created PostScript, a stack-based programming language, at Adobe; it shipped in 1984.
Co-designed SQL, originally SEQUEL, at IBM with Raymond Boyce in 1974.
Wrote the KornShell (ksh) at Bell Labs, announced in 1983.
Leads the MIT Media Lab group that created Scratch, launched in 2007.
Designed FORMAC at IBM and served on the committee that defined COBOL in 1959.
Edited the ALGOL 60 report; he is the N in Backus-Naur form.
Designed BCPL at Cambridge in 1967, an ancestor of B and C.
Designed SASL, KRC and Miranda, the lazy functional language that most influenced Haskell.
MIT professor who co-created Julia; its four creators announced it in a 2012 blog post.
Created Gleam, a statically typed language for the Erlang VM; version 1.0 shipped in 2024.
Led the PLT group that created Racket, originally PLT Scheme, starting in 1995.
Created Idris, a dependently typed language, and co-created the Whitespace esolang.
Created Roc, a functional language inspired by Elm; also wrote Elm in Action.
Wrote the Monad Manifesto in 2002, which became Windows PowerShell.
Co-created Processing with Ben Fry at the MIT Media Lab in 2001.
Co-created Processing with Casey Reas in 2001 as a sketchbook language for visual artists.
Led the design of CPL in the 1960s, whose simplification BCPL led to B and C.
Created PL/M for Intel microprocessors in 1973, then used it to write CP/M.
Wrote UnrealScript, the scripting language of the original Unreal Engine.
Created Vim and its Vim script language, and the experimental Zimbu language.
Founding member of the committee that designed Haskell and a longtime Yale professor.
Joined Walter Bright as co-designer of D in 2006 and wrote The D Programming Language.
Announced the experimental Carbon language as a C++ successor at CppNorth in 2022.
Co-created Dart at Google with Lars Bak; both previously worked on V8.
Created the Wren scripting language and Lox, the language built in his book Crafting Interpreters.
Created Nim, originally named Nimrod, first released in 2008.
Created Hare, a systems language announced in 2022; also wrote the Sway compositor.
Created REBOL in 1997; earlier designed the Exec kernel of AmigaOS.
Created React at Facebook, then ReasonML, an alternative syntax for OCaml, in 2016.
Created Haxe, first released in 2005, which compiles to many target languages.
Created the Lean theorem prover and programming language at Microsoft Research in 2013.
Co-created Prolog with Alain Colmerauer in Marseille in 1972.
Proposed Solidity in 2014 as an Ethereum co-founder; later founded Polkadot.
The W in AWK, written at Bell Labs in 1977 with Aho and Kernighan.
Developed sed, the Unix stream editor and its scripting language, at Bell Labs in 1973-74.
Led the MIT group that developed Cilk, a multithreaded extension of C, in the 1990s.
Co-created the prototype-based language Self with Randall Smith at Xerox PARC in 1986.
Created Newspeak and co-authored the Java Language Specification; also worked on Dart.
Co-created SNOBOL at Bell Labs in 1962, then designed Icon at the University of Arizona.
Designed Concurrent Pascal in 1975, an early language built around monitors.
Designed occam for the Inmos transputer, released in 1983.
Served on the ALGOL 58 and ALGOL 60 committees; first Turing Award recipient, 1966.
Led the design of ALGOL 68 and devised the two-level grammar used to define it.
Co-created INTERCAL at Princeton in 1972 with James Lyon; also expanded Colossal Cave Adventure.
Created the array languages A+, K and q; K underlies the kdb+ database.
Led the Carnegie Mellon project behind Alice, an educational language for 3D animation.
Co-created Logo in 1967 with Seymour Papert and Wally Feurzeig at BBN.
Co-created Logo at Bolt, Beranek and Newman in 1967.
Co-founded Adobe with John Warnock in 1982 and co-created PostScript.
Co-designed SEQUEL, later SQL, with Donald Chamberlin; also the Boyce in Boyce-Codd normal form.
Co-created Objective-C with Brad Cox in the early 1980s.
One of the four co-creators of Julia and a co-founder of Julia Computing.
One of Erlang's three original designers at Ericsson, with Joe Armstrong and Mike Williams.
Led the Xerox PARC team that created AspectJ and coined aspect-oriented programming.
Co-created the prototype-based language Self with David Ungar at Xerox PARC in 1986.
Co-created SNOBOL at Bell Labs in 1962 with Ralph Griswold and Ivan Polonsky.
Credited with writing the first assembly language, for the ARC computers at Birkbeck in the late 1940s.
Wrote Autocode for the Manchester Mark 1 in 1952, often called the first compiled language.
Developed Mark 1 Autocode for the Ferranti Mark 1 in the mid-1950s and later co-created the Compiler Compiler.
Led the design team for Ada 95 and later created the parallel language ParaSail.
Designed Planner at MIT in 1969 and later developed the actor model of computation.
Created TRAC, a text-processing macro language, in the 1960s; also coined information retrieval.
Created JOVIAL in the late 1950s; the name stands for Jules' Own Version of IAL.
Created SETL at NYU around 1969, a language built on mathematical set theory.
Co-developed MUMPS at Massachusetts General Hospital in 1966 and later founded Meditech.
Created Ceylon at Red Hat, announced in 2011; earlier created Hibernate.
Designed HyperTalk, the scripting language of Apple's HyperCard, released in 1987.
Created Inform in 1993 for text adventures; Inform 7 source reads like English prose.
Created Esterel, a synchronous language for reactive systems, in the early 1980s.
Co-created INTERCAL in 1972 with Don Woods, designed to resemble no other language.
Created Befunge in 1993, a two-dimensional language designed to be hard to compile.
Created Malbolge in 1998; the first working program took about two years and a search algorithm.
Created Piet, whose programs are abstract images, and Chef, whose programs read like recipes.
Created LOLCODE in 2007, with keywords like HAI and KTHXBYE.
Co-created the J language with Kenneth Iverson, first released in 1990.
Designed Alef, a concurrent language for Plan 9 from Bell Labs.
Created FALSE in 1993, whose tiny compiler inspired Brainfuck; later made Lobster.
Wrote the first version of zsh in 1990 while a student at Princeton.
Created fish, the friendly interactive shell, first released in 2005.
Co-created Lua in 1993 at PUC-Rio with Roberto Ierusalimschy and Waldemar Celes.
Co-created Lua at the Tecgraf group of PUC-Rio in 1993.
One of Erlang's three original designers at Ericsson in 1986, with Joe Armstrong and Robert Virding.
Started Crystal in 2011 at Manas, aiming for Ruby-like syntax with static types.
Created V, a compiled language first released publicly in 2019.
Designed Pony, an actor-model language using reference capabilities for safe concurrency.
Created Io in 2002, a prototype-based language influenced by Self and Smalltalk.
Created Factor in 2003, a concatenative stack-based language.
Created Joy at La Trobe University, a purely functional concatenative language.
Co-created Unison, a language where code is identified by a hash of its content.
Created Koka at Microsoft Research, a language that tracks algebraic effects in its types.
Designed Agda 2, a dependently typed language, as his PhD work at Chalmers.
Created PureScript in 2013, a Haskell-like language that compiles to JavaScript.
Co-designed the Arc Lisp dialect with Paul Graham; also known for the 1988 Morris worm.

nope.Linus Torvalds: He wrote the Linux kernel and Git, not a programming language.
nope.Ada Lovelace: Ada is named in her honor; she wrote an early algorithm, not a language.
nope.Haskell Curry: Haskell was named after him years after his death; he did not design it.
nope.Blaise Pascal: Pascal was named after the 17th-century mathematician; Niklaus Wirth designed it.
nope.Bill Gates: He co-wrote Altair BASIC, an interpreter for a language Kemeny and Kurtz created.
nope.Ryan Dahl: Node.js and Deno are JavaScript runtimes, not new languages.
nope.Tim Berners-Lee: HTML is a markup language, not a programming language.
nope.Edgar Codd: He invented the relational model; SQL was designed by Chamberlin and Boyce.
nope.Margaret Hamilton: She led the Apollo flight software team but did not create a language.

traps.q: Who began a hobby language project over Christmas 1989 and named it after a British comedy troupe?
traps.l: Python's name comes from Monty Python's Flying Circus, not the snake.

traps.q: Who wrote the first prototype of a language at Netscape in about ten days in May 1995?
traps.l: The language was called Mocha and then LiveScript before shipping as JavaScript.
